    Settings & help

    Live traffic & owner access

    Sign in with GitHub as Arthur-Freedom, then press Refresh traffic. The server checks the owner's numeric GitHub ID before requesting Google traffic for all five stations. Other visitors cannot request paid traffic, even by calling the service directly.

    Each refresh measures congestion along one fixed road approach to each station, up to the final kilometre. The coloured approach lines appear on the Google map. A shorter red length ranks as less busy. Routes describe car traffic; motorcycle queues and congestion inside the station may differ.

    Refreshes have a 15-minute cooldown and a maximum of ten per Bali day, shared across devices. Optional auto-refresh runs only while this tab is visible. Five successful traffic requests cost about US$0.075 after Google's monthly free allowance; the Google map has its own free allowance. Failed attempts also consume a refresh slot.

    The reading time is when Google was queried. Google combines recent traffic signals and estimates; this is not an exact observation time for every vehicle. Failed readings retain their original time and are labelled. Sign-out removes the live readings from this view. Reloading the page does not request paid traffic automatically.

    Busyness & expected waits

    The comparison uses Less busy below 250 m of congested approach road, Busy from 250–899 m, and Very busy at 900 m or more. These are rough comparison bands. Red roads can be caused by junctions and through traffic as well as a fuel queue.

    Actual waiting minutes appear only when reported. Unknown waits stay unknown. Reports up to 15 minutes rank as less busy, 16–45 as busy, and above 45 as very busy, using the midpoint. Opening and fuel reports expire for ranking after an hour; refreshing road traffic never renews those reports.

    The public fallback displays dated manual observations. Old readings say “Was…” and cannot become a current recommendation. Reload saved data only reloads that fallback. The optional queue calculator is a scenario, not a measured wait.

    Your checks and privacy

    Use Add your check on a station to record what you see. These checks and your selected starting point stay in this browser. Owner sign-in is shared with the cinema app on this GitHub Pages origin; signing out revokes that device session for both apps. Google traffic readings stay in memory and are not saved to GitHub or browser storage. The server keeps refresh counts and times to enforce limits. Google receives fixed station approach coordinates, not your selected starting point. They are not sent to other visitors. A newer published observation takes priority over an older personal check. Checks saved on the original Sites address do not transfer to this address.

    Your location is requested only when you press “Use my location”. Directions open Google Maps with the starting point you selected.

    Distances and waiting estimates

    Distances are straight-line distances from your selected starting point. Driving routes can be longer.

    The optional waiting calculator assumes that the entire entered red stretch is a motorbike queue. It estimates bikes ahead from spacing and rows, then divides by the combined service rate of the active pumps. All inputs are adjustable. It excludes any queue inside the station and cannot account for an empty tank at the station or a stopped pump.

    Coverage, sources & terms

    Google Maps use is subject to Google Maps terms and Google privacy policy. This independent tool provides indicative comparisons without guaranteeing fuel availability, opening hours or waiting times.

    Five mapped stations around Nusa Dua and Jimbaran. Unchecked stations are left unranked. Fuel availability is unknown until someone records a check; every report can become outdated.

    Station names, coordinates and traffic observations: Google Maps. Live traffic and live basemap: Google Maps. Public fallback basemap: OpenFreeMap / OpenStreetMap. This is an independent comparison tool.
